## Genome Bin Quality Assessment Using CheckM

Following genome binning with MetaBAT2, the quality of the reconstructed genome bins was assessed using CheckM. CheckM estimates genome completeness and contamination based on the presence and copy number of lineage-specific marker genes.

The purpose of this step was to identify genome bins suitable for further taxonomic classification and functional analysis of the Black Band Disease (BBD) microbial community.

### Preparation of Genome Bins

The longest contig from the Flye assembly, `contig_113` (4,706,700 bp), was extracted as a separate FASTA file following the workshop instructions. This allowed the longest contig to be assessed independently alongside the MetaBAT2 bins.

The 70 MetaBAT2 bins and the additional contig were copied into the `checkm/bins_bbd/` directory, resulting in 71 FASTA files for quality assessment.

### CheckM Results

CheckM was run using the `lineage_wf` workflow to estimate genome completeness and contamination.

The following results were obtained for the six most complete bins:

| Bin | Marker lineage | Completeness (%) | Contamination (%) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| contig_113 | Cytophagales | 97.62 | 1.64 |
| metabat.40 | Cyanobacteria | 97.56 | 0.67 |
| metabat.41 | Bacteria | 31.03 | 0.00 |
| metabat.69 | Bacteria | 30.28 | 0.00 |
| metabat.2 | Bacteria | 29.31 | 0.00 |
| metabat.29 | Deltaproteobacteria | 28.18 | 0.13 |

The two most complete bins were `contig_113` (97.62%) and `metabat.40` (97.56%), both with estimated contamination below 2%. The next most complete bin, `metabat.41`, had only 31.03% completeness.

These results suggest that the first two bins contain substantially more complete genomic information than the remaining bins. Their marker lineages suggest associations with Cytophagales and Cyanobacteria, respectively, although further taxonomic classification is required.

### Selection of Bins for Further Analysis

Following the workshop instructions, bins with estimated completeness greater than 15% were selected for subsequent analysis.

A total of **17 bins** met the completeness threshold and were recorded in `bbd_topbins.txt`.

Although only two bins had completeness above 97%, the additional selected bins may still provide useful information about the BBD microbial community. These selected bins were subsequently used for taxonomic classification with GTDB-Tk and functional annotation with Prokka and MinPath.

### Processing Log

First, the longest contig was identified from the Flye assembly and extracted as a separate FASTA file:

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm

cat ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print length($seq),$name}' | sort -n | tail

samtools faidx ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta contig_113 > ../metabat/bins_bbd/contig_113.fa
```

The MetaBAT2 bins and the longest contig were copied into the CheckM input directory:

```{bash}
cp ../metabat/bins_bbd/*.fa bins_bbd/
```

CheckM was then run through the SLURM scheduler using the script [run_checkm_bbd.sh](checkm/run_checkm_bbd.sh).

The main analysis command in the script was:

```{bash}
checkm lineage_wf bins_bbd out -t 6 -x fa -f checkm_results_bbd.txt
```

The `lineage_wf` option ran the lineage-specific marker gene analysis, `-t 6` used six processing threads, `-x fa` specified the FASTA file extension, and `-f` saved the results to `checkm_results_bbd.txt`.

The job was submitted using:

```{bash}
sbatch run_checkm_bbd.sh
```

The CheckM results were examined, and bins with completeness greater than 15% were selected:

```{bash}
head -n 20 checkm_results_bbd.txt

cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}' > bbd_topbins.txt

wc -l bbd_topbins.txt
```

The resulting `bbd_topbins.txt` file contained 17 bin identifiers for the subsequent analyses.
